summary: Query Records: fetches records of a cloud database class with filter/sort/limit, keeps results live, and outputs them as an array.
description: Query Records reads a class from the connected cloud database and exposes the matching records on `items` (an array of record objects), with `count`, `firstItemId` and `isEmpty` alongside. The query — class name, visual or JavaScript filter, sorting, limit and pagination — is configured in the node's parameters. Results are live by default: when a record elsewhere in the app is created, saved or deleted, the node re-checks it against the current query and updates `items` in place. `fetched` fires when a fetch completes, `failure`/`error` report problems.
whenToUse: The starting point of every cloud-data list or lookup in browser logic. For writing data use Create/Save/Delete New Record nodes; for a single record by id use Model2/DbModel2; in cloud functions querying is available too (availableIn: cloud).

ports.items: Array output with the query result; the canonical source for a Repeater's `items`.
ports.fetched: Signal; fires each time a fetch (initial or re-run) completes.
ports.isEmpty: Boolean level; drive empty-state visuals from here rather than comparing `count` yourself.
ports.realtime: Boolean. Turns on Subscribe To Changes: the node holds a live subscription on the collection and re-runs this query when any client creates, updates or deletes a record. Off by default. ⚠️ The port is declared whatever the backend is and is never hidden — a backend that cannot push says why on `realtimeError` instead. For reacting to changes without owning a query, use the standalone Subscribe To Changes node.
ports.subscribed: True only while the subscription is confirmed live — false during connect, during backoff, and after a fatal auth failure. Wire it to an indicator's visibility so people can see when live updates are actually running.
ports.realtimeStatus: Which state the subscription is in as a string: connecting, subscribed, interrupted or unavailable. `subscribed` alone cannot tell 'reconnecting' from 'never started'.
ports.realtimeError: Last connection or protocol error; cleared when a subscription (re)confirms. An invalid token is fatal and the node will not retry until a parameter changes.
ports.realtimeFailure: Fires when the subscription fails in a way it will not recover from on its own.
ports.created: Fires once per remote create batch, after the Changed outputs have updated.
ports.updated: Fires once per remote update batch, after the Changed outputs have updated.
ports.deleted: Fires once per remote delete batch. ⚠️ Delete events carry only primary keys, so `changedRecord` is null and `changedRecords` holds key strings.
ports.changed: Fires alongside every created/updated/deleted. Wire this when any change should trigger the same reaction — most often back into this node's own `Do` to re-fetch.
ports.changedEvent: The last event kind as a string: create, update or delete.
ports.changedRecord: First record of the last create/update batch; null for deletes.
ports.changedRecords: All records of the last batch; for deletes, an array of primary-key strings.
ports.changedRecordId: Primary key of the first affected record, across all three event types.

runtimeBehavior: All *inputs* are runtime-determined (runtime-discovered + editor-adapter): the class choice, filter values, sort keys and paging inputs are generated from the project's database schema and the visual filter you build in the editor — e.g. each 'value' placeholder in a filter becomes its own input port, and actions like fetch ('storageFetch') are registered on demand. A generator cannot enumerate them statically; an authoring tool should set `collectionName` and filter parameters, and may wire signals to fetch-related inputs which the runtime registers when used.
patterns: `items` → Repeater `items`, with record properties delivered to the item component via Component Inputs: the canonical list page.
Event Receiver `eventReceived` → fetch input: re-run a query on demand from anywhere in the app.

Turn on Subscribe To Changes and wire `Changed` back into this node's own `Do`: the list stays current without polling, on every backend whose descriptor allows it — SSE on the built-in backend and PocketBase, a WebSocket on Directus.
`Subscribed` → a status indicator's visibility, so people can see when live updates are actually running rather than assuming.
antiPatterns: Re-querying on a timer to feel 'live' — results already update from cloud events; explicit re-fetch is only needed when the server changed outside those events.
Treating `Changed Record` as the full record on a delete — delete events carry only primary keys, so it is null and only `Changed Record Id` is populated.
Polling with a Timer while Subscribe To Changes is available on this backend. Subscribe and re-fetch on `Changed` instead.
Assuming `Subscribed` distinguishes 'reconnecting' from 'never connected' — it does not. Read `Realtime Status` for that.
